site.title: The Week After Christmas
site.subtitle: Five places we're kicking around for the week after Christmas. Sunday December 27, 2026 to Sunday January 3, 2027.
site.disclaimer: These are rough ideas. Nothing is booked or decided. Prices are rough guesses for ten of us at holiday-week rates unless they say published, and the flight days are what the airlines announced, so they still need checking for our dates.
site.party: Mom, Patrick and Sara, Andrew and Trisha, Kristina and Michael with Bennett (7) and Taylor (3), and Daniel. Seven of us would fly from Norfolk, two from Richmond and one from Austin.
rules: One house for all of us, ideally with a bedroom for each couple, Mom, Daniel and the kids. Six bedrooms, or five plus a good bunk room.
Somewhere we could walk out the door into a town with things to do, plus cars for the group, rather than a compound.
Mom's idea of a good week: a nice place to stay, places to walk, one plan a day, splitting up for things and getting back together for dinner.
A kitchen at the house and maybe a chef night or two, keeping the couple of allergies in the family in mind.
Some of us might want to ski, surf or dive most days and some of us might want easier days with the kids. The idea would be room for both from the same house, with everyone together for dinner.

trips.name: Belize
trips.pitch: A barefoot little fishing-village town on a thin strip of sand, with the barrier reef out front and jungle, Maya ruins and howler monkeys an hour or two inland. The idea would be a six-bedroom beach house with a pool, a pier, kayaks, golf carts and a chef included every other day, and a short hop on a small plane from the international airport so we never go into Belize City. Mom and whoever is certified could dive a reef she hasn't done yet, and the kids would have calm water inside the reef, a little island beach day and the monkeys. There's no surf, though, and the house we found is 8 miles up the road from the village.
why: The diving and snorkeling might be the most of any of the options. The Silk Cayes and Glover's Reef are day boats from the house for Mom and whoever is certified, with the snorkelers on the same boat, and Laughing Bird Caye is a national park 11 miles out.

It's the only one with jungle and ruins too: Monkey River for howler monkeys and manatees, the Cockscomb jaguar preserve trails, and the Maya sites at Nim Li Punit and Lubaantun about two hours' drive south.

Mission Bay, the house we'd probably ask about first, has six bedrooms with a real bunk room, a pool by the sand, a pier, kayaks and a golf cart, and a chef comes with the rent for one full day out of every two. It's rated 9.8 out of 10 from 102 reviews.

Placencia Village has a pedestrian Sidewalk about three quarters of a mile long, with cafes, gelato, little shops and restaurants. From the house you could also walk to the Naia spa, the Maya Beach bistro and Inky's Mini Golf.
The water stays warm, about 81 degrees, and inside the reef it's flat and shallow for the kids.
Roughly $27,000 to $58,000 for ten, with the house as the big unknown since no holiday rate is posted yet.
catch: It's the longest travel day of the options, about 10.5 to 13.5 hours each way. One connection into Belize City, then a 25 to 45 minute flight on a small plane to the Placencia airstrip. Mom might count that hop as a second stop.

The State Department has Belize at Level 2, Exercise Increased Caution, for crime, reissued March 12, 2026. The Level 3 area is Southside Belize City, which we wouldn't go near. Worth reading the advisory ourselves, the link is below.

A state of emergency ran from May 8 to about early June 2026 in Belize City and Belize District, including Ladyville, where the international airport is. It ended (the UK took its notice down June 12) and we found no renewal through October 21. Placencia was never part of it, and we'd stay inside the airport between flights.

On the peninsula itself: in February 2025 a US developer was shot dead outside his villa project at Cocoplum on Maya Beach, which police called a targeted hit tied to a fraud dispute. That's the same development Mission Bay is in. In March 2026 a man was stabbed to death by a neighbor in the Maya Beach area, which police said was not gang-related. In October 2023 armed men tied up the guard at the Placencia airstrip and stole a small plane, which crashed, and police suspected a drug flight. In March 2023 robbers hit a beach house at a Seine Bight resort and traded fire with police, with no one hurt. We found no 2026 shootings in Placencia.

Medical care is thin. The Placencia Polyclinic near the airstrip is billed as 24-hour, though local reporting found it unstaffed on one visit, and it's about 8 miles from the house. The nearest hospital is in Dangriga, about 1 to 1.5 hours away, and anything serious would mean a flight to Belize City. We'd bring epinephrine from home.
No six-bedroom house turned up inside the village walk. Mission Bay is 8 miles north, roughly 25 to 35 minutes by golf cart by our guess, on the one peninsula road, which is unlit at night.
No surf to speak of, since the reef blocks the swell.
December northers can bring a gray, windy day or two and cancel the outer-reef boat days. 2026 has also been a record sargassum year, and the east-facing beaches where the houses sit can get seaweed.
The Blue Hole is 3.5 hours each way by boat from Placencia, so that would be a long day just for the certified divers.
Every house is request-only or shows no calendar for December 27 to January 3, and late October is late to be asking about a holiday six-bedroom.
trips.weather: Warm and mostly sunny, with highs around 81, nights around 68 to 72 and the sea about 81. Expect passing showers most days, with sources disagreeing on how much rain (somewhere from 3 to 7 inches over the month). Now and then a norther comes through and makes it cooler, breezy and choppy for a day or two. Late December is the start of the busy season.

notes.title: What about Ambergris Caye?
paragraphs: The reef starts right at the dock of a six-bedroom villa with a pool, Hol Chan and Shark Ray Alley are about 15 minutes away by boat, and Mom could reach the Blue Hole in about two hours instead of three and a half, so it would probably be the easier dive week. The hop from the international airport is only 15 minutes, and the island has a private hospital with a decompression chamber. Town is a 15 to 20 minute golf-cart ride, a bit closer than Placencia but still not a walk. The island has had a rougher 2026 for crime, which we'd want to read up on, and the house we found has mixed reviews. Roughly $28,500 to $49,000 for ten, with no holiday rate posted for the house yet.

getting_there.how: No nonstop. One connection into Belize City through Charlotte (American flies Charlotte to Belize daily), Atlanta (Delta) or Miami (American). Kayak shows the shortest one-stop trip at about 6 hours 43 minutes. Then the small-plane hop to Placencia from the same terminal. The earliest morning flight out would give us the most room to make the hop.
getting_there.est: About $850 to $1,300 a seat, our guess for the holidays (Kayak's December median is $829)

getting_there.how: No nonstop. One connection through Miami, Atlanta (shortest average about 7 hours 12 minutes), Houston or Charlotte, then the hop to Placencia.
getting_there.est: About $850 to $1,300 a seat, our guess

getting_there.how: One connection through Houston (United from Bush, Southwest from Hobby), Dallas (American) or Miami, then the hop to Placencia.

Tropic Air and Maya Island Air fly from the international airport to the Placencia airstrip in 25 to 45 minutes, depending on whether they stop in Dangriga. The trackers disagree on how many flights a day (2 to 5 a day on one, about 9 a week on another), so a morning arrival in Belize City would help. The planes are small, so bags are limited, which matters with dive gear, and we'd ask Tropic Air for a group quote. The other way is about a 3.5-hour drive by van, skipping Belize City on the Burrell Boom road, with the Belize Zoo on the way. At the house, golf carts and taxis. Belize is an hour behind Eastern time in winter.
getting_there.est: Tropic Air round trips seen at $198 to $290 for non-holiday dates, a van for ten would need a quote

houses.name: Mission Bay (Gecko Vacation Rentals)
houses.detail: Six bedrooms and 5 baths in Cocoplum near Maya Beach. The listing shows four kings, a queen and a twin-bunk room, plus a twin daybed in the top-floor suite, though its two bed lists don't match. Sleeps 12 with a cap of 10 adults, so the 8 adults and 2 kids fit. A freshwater pool by the sand (the listing also mentions an infinity pool out back), a pier with a palapa, kayaks, paddleboards and one 4-seat golf cart, walled and gated. A chef comes with the house for one full day for every two nights, groceries at cost, with extra chef days at $125. It's on three floors with stairs and the main suite on the top floor, so we'd ask which bedrooms are on the ground floor and whether the pool is fenced. About 8 miles to the village, with the Naia spa and Inky's Mini Golf a short walk. 9.8 out of 10 from 102 reviews.
houses.price: From $768 a night on Vrbo, but that's a one-night October quote for two adults. No holiday rate or calendar posted for the week
houses.verdict: The one we'd probably call first. It's the six-bedroom we could confirm in detail, with a real bunk room, and the chef comes with it.

houses.name: Maya Alux (Dream Exotic Rentals)
houses.detail: Six bedrooms: four king suites on the main floor and a two-bedroom apartment upstairs with a queen and a full-over-full bunk room. Four baths, some shared, sleeps 14. A beachfront pool, a rooftop terrace, kayaks, paddleboards, bikes and a gym, with daily maid, laundry, a 6-seat golf cart and one airport transfer included. The listing only says Placencia, so we don't know how far it is from the village. Dream Exotic says the chef is extra and Expedia says it's included.
houses.price: From $1,200 a night in low season, holiday rate not posted. Request only, 4 to 7 night minimum
houses.verdict: Could be a good second call, once we find out where on the peninsula it actually is.

houses.name: Island Breeze Villa, Placencia Caye (Dream Exotic Rentals)
houses.detail: Five bedrooms on a little island across from the village: four kings and a kids' room with four single beds, sleeps 14. A rooftop pool with a bar, a private sandy beach on the calm side for swimming and snorkeling, kayaks and paddleboards. A chef three days a week is included, food extra, plus a caretaker, maid and laundry. A shuttle boat gets to the village dock in about 2 minutes. The listings disagree on the number of bathrooms.
houses.price: From $750 a night in low season, holiday rate not posted. Request only
houses.verdict: Closest to town of anything we found, but it's one bedroom short and every trip in is a boat ride.

houses.name: Casa Corazon (Top Villas)
houses.detail: Six bedrooms including a casita, with a king, four queens and a twin-over-double bunk, 4.5 baths, sleeps 14 per Top Villas. Vacasa lists what looks like the same house as five bedrooms for 10, so the layout needs checking. An infinity pool, a private pier with a palapa and beachfront on the northern part of the peninsula, a short drive to the village and about 5 km from Maya Beach. A chef three days for a weekly stay, food extra.
houses.price: From $898 a night, holiday rate not posted
houses.verdict: Worth asking about if the first two are taken, though it's farther from everything.

houses.name: Conmigo Villas, Maya Beach
houses.detail: Six bedrooms and 6 baths in two connected units, each with its own kitchen, sleeps 20. A pool with a poolside bar, beachfront, a private pier and kayaks. A listing says a private chef is included. About 7 to 8 miles from the village.
houses.price: Not shown online for the week
houses.verdict: Two units side by side, so we'd be split a bit. Price and dates would take a phone call.

agenda.all: The earliest flights out of Norfolk, Richmond and Austin, one connection into Belize City by early afternoon, and the little plane down to Placencia. Golf carts at the house, the pool and an easy dinner.
Dinner at the house.
agenda.crew: A half-day of flats or reef fishing in the afternoon.
agenda.relax: A pool and beach morning, then golf carts into the village for lunch, the Sidewalk and gelato at Tutti Frutti.

agenda.all: A private boat out to Laughing Bird Caye, snorkeling and a beach picnic, back by mid-afternoon for Taylor's nap. Bennett could snorkel in a vest and Taylor could play on the sand. First chef day.

agenda.crew: A two-tank dive at the Silk Cayes for Mom and whoever is certified, with the snorkelers on the same boat. Or the Blue Hole day for the certified divers, 3.5 hours each way.
agenda.relax: The Naia spa for whoever wants it. Kids at the pool and Inky's Mini Golf.

agenda.all: Monkey River in the morning for howler monkeys, manatees and birds, maybe a shorter private trip so it isn't too long for Taylor. New Year's Eve dinner at the house with the chef.
A slow day, and if a norther knocked out a boat day earlier, this could be the makeup day.
agenda.crew: Glover's Reef dives for Mom and whoever is certified, or an offshore fishing trip.
agenda.relax: Beach and pool at the house, kayaks on the calm lagoon side, or the Sidewalk end to end with coffee at Brewed Awakenings.

agenda.all: A farewell dinner with the chef.
agenda.crew: The Maya ruins at Nim Li Punit and Lubaantun, about two hours' drive, with lunch in Toledo. Or the Moho Caye day sail.
agenda.relax: Che'il chocolate-making in Maya Center with the kids, and maybe a waterfall swim and the Cockscomb trails on the way.

agenda.all: A morning swim, the little plane back to Belize City and one connection home.

trips.name: Puerto Rico
trips.place: Isla Verde, on the beach just east of San Juan
trips.pitch: A week on what seems like the calmest sand beach around San Juan, in a six-bedroom pool house about three minutes' walk from the water and roughly ten minutes from the airport, so no long drive at either end. Pine Grove, at the west end of Isla Verde, sits behind a reef well offshore that takes the edge off the winter swell, so on most days the kids could wade with a grownup close by and the adults could swim. The walk out the door is a busy hotel and restaurant avenue, with casinos and some chains mixed in, rather than a little town square, so Old San Juan, about 20 to 25 minutes away, would be our walking day. The surfers would have reef breaks 10 to 20 minutes from the house, the dive boats, the catamaran, the bio bay and El Yunque are out east toward Fajardo, and there are calm-water spots in the city for the big-swell days.
why: The beach at the door might be the calmest sand in the San Juan area. Pine Grove is a sand beach and sandbar break, with the reef sitting well offshore around a little cay, and surf-forecast.com says it's too small to surf 73 percent of the time in December. That should mean a gentle shore most days.
Balneario de Carolina, about a kilometer east along the same beach, has lifeguards and a small kids' water park. It's listed as open Tuesday to Sunday, 8 to 5, and closed Mondays.

Villa Violeta and Villa Catalina are six-bedroom houses with private pools, about 3 minutes on foot from Pine Grove and 2 to 9 minutes from restaurants. Both are rated 9.6 out of 10, and Catalina has a real bunk room for the kids.
The JetBlue nonstop from Norfolk lands about ten minutes from the house, so there's no long transfer at either end.

The surfers could drive about 10 minutes to Aviones or 20 to La Ocho, Mom and whoever is certified could do a two-tank boat dive out of Fajardo, and the same coast has the Icacos catamaran, the bio bay and El Yunque. Old San Juan's forts and streets are about 20 to 25 minutes away.
On a big-swell day there are calm-water spots in the city, at Escambrón, Playita del Condado and the Condado Lagoon, about 15 to 20 minutes west.
US soil, with dollars, phones and US hospitals about 15 minutes away.
Roughly $28,000 to $54,000 for ten, with the house as the big unknown since no holiday rate is posted.
catch: The walk out the door is a resort avenue, not a town. Isla Verde Avenue mixes some good local places with hotel casinos and chains like Denny's and Burger King, so the strolling-around-town part of the week would be Old San Juan.

Pine Grove itself has no lifeguards. They're at Balneario de Carolina, a short walk east, and we couldn't open the page with its hours, so we'd confirm them. On the Pine Grove sand, a grownup would want to stay within arm's reach of Taylor.

Nobody we found has described the seabed itself. Some guides mention scattered shells and small rocks in places, so water shoes for the kids and a look along the waterline on the first day seem like a good idea.

Late December is the middle of north-swell season, and a big swell still reaches the bay. On a high rip-current day (the National Weather Service posts it every morning), the swim would move to Escambrón, Playita del Condado or the lagoon, a 15 to 20 minute drive. Ocean Park, Condado and Piñones nearby aren't December beaches for little ones. The weather service lists rip-current deaths at all three, including Ocean Park on January 1, 2026, though we haven't double-checked those tables.
The surf at the door is small most of December, clean only about 5 percent of the time, so it's more for a lesson on a small day. The surfers would mostly drive to Aviones or La Ocho.

No holiday rate, minimum stay or calendar showed on any of the houses. Three of them look like they share an owner, so one inquiry might price all three, but if that owner is booked, all three are. A holiday rate over $3,000 a night would push the top of the budget toward $60,000.

Villa Catalina has one recent 4 out of 10 review that mentioned the air conditioning not working, a dirty pool and a slow host. None of the houses confirms a pool fence, though one Catalina photo caption mentions a white one.
The houses are right next to the airport, so there might be jet noise. That's our guess, since no listing or review we read mentions it.

The dive boats leave from Fajardo, about an hour each way by our estimate, and December swell can cancel them. We don't know yet whether non-divers can ride along. The Icacos catamaran needs 12 people to sail a shared trip, so we'd either charter it for the ten of us or join another group.

New Year's week is busy. Pine Grove and the balneario are among the most crowded beaches in the metro area, El Yunque's El Portal visitor center is closed on New Year's Day, and the La Mina trail is closed for construction.

For walks after dinner, one guide calls the Isla Verde hotel zone generally safe, thinning out toward the highway, so we'd keep to the lit avenue and the hotel fronts and stay off the beach late. Carolina closed the avenue to through traffic late on Thursday to Sunday nights after some incidents, but the article is undated, so it may not still be in place.
Sargassum and Portuguese man o' war are possible, and all the drive times here are our estimates, since we haven't mapped them.
trips.weather: Highs around 83, lows around 73 to 74, and about 2.8 inches of rain over roughly six days in December, usually passing showers. The sea is about 81 to 82 degrees. Late December is the heart of north-swell season, so we'd expect a big-swell day or two, and the trade winds usually pick up by late morning, so mornings would be the time to swim and surf.

notes.title: What about Luquillo?
paragraphs: We spent a while on Luquillo, out on the northeast coast about 45 minutes from the airport. Its big public beach, Balneario La Monserrate, comes up everywhere as calm and shallow behind an offshore reef, with lifeguards. Right next to it is the kiosk strip, about sixty little open-air restaurants, which looked like a lot of fun for lunches. El Yunque would be about 10 minutes away and the Fajardo boats about 30.

The thing we kept bumping into is that the six-bedroom house on Playa Fortuna loses most of its own sand in the winter, and one guest had to climb over boulders to get to the water. So the swimming beach would be a 15 to 20 minute walk, or a quick drive once you add the kids and the beach gear. If a big house turns up closer to the balneario, we might look at it again.

notes.title: What about Dorado?
paragraphs: We also looked at Dorado, about 40 minutes west of the airport, where the Ritz-Carlton Reserve and some beautiful villas are. The public beach there, Nolo Morales, is sand with a roped swim area and lifeguards. It faces the winter north swell straight on, though, so we could see several red-flag days in our week, and the beaches right in front of the villas aren't really meant for swimming.

The villas we found open for our dates were five bedrooms and ran about $22,000 to $44,000 for the house alone. They're in a gated resort where you'd mostly drive or take a golf cart to dinner. It feels more like a pool-and-resort week than a beach week, which could be nice on a different trip.

getting_there.how: JetBlue nonstop to San Juan, announced for Mon, Wed, Fri and Sun (flight 929 out, 928 back). Sunday Dec 27 out and Sunday Jan 3 back fit that pattern. The clock times differ between sources, so we'd check jetblue.com.

The JetBlue nonstop flies Tue, Thu and Sat, so Andrew and Trisha could drive to Norfolk and fly with everyone, fly Sat Dec 26 and Sat Jan 2 with a hotel night (the Isla Verde hotels are minutes from the gate), or connect once on the Sundays.
One stop on the Sundays, with American through Charlotte or Dallas, Delta through Atlanta or United through Houston. Southwest's seasonal Austin nonstop isn't confirmed for the holidays.

Two seven-seat vehicles from the airport, which is about 5 to 10 minutes from the Isla Verde houses. Ocean Park is about 15 minutes, Old San Juan about 20 to 25, the Fajardo marinas about an hour and El Yunque about 45 minutes. Those drive times are our estimates.

houses.name: Villa Catalina, Isla Verde (Vrbo)
houses.detail: Six bedrooms, five with queens plus a bunk room with four twin beds, 4 baths, sleeps 14. A private pool, and one photo caption mentions a white fence around it, which we'd want to confirm. On the map Pine Grove is about 3 minutes on foot (the description says 1), with Denny's 2 minutes away, Casa Cuba and Metropol 3, Lupi's 4 and La Bodeguita 7. A generator, a water cistern and air conditioning throughout. 9.6 out of 10 from 86 reviews, though one recent 4 out of 10 review mentioned the air conditioning not working, a dirty pool and a slow host.
houses.price: From $1,024 for one October night with taxes and fees on Vrbo. Our guess for the holiday week is $1,600 to $2,800 a night
houses.verdict: The one we'd probably ask about first, since the bunk room is a real kids' room. We'd ask the host about that recent review.

houses.name: Villa Violeta, Isla Verde (Vrbo)

Isla Verde Beach about 6 minutes on foot and restaurants within about 14. A garage for one car plus a driveway for six. No generator mentioned. 8.8 out of 10 from 56 reviews, renters 25 and up.

houses.verdict: Lots of room and parking, though a little farther from the restaurants and no mention of backup power.

houses.name: Villa Stephanie, Ocean Park (Vrbo)
houses.detail: Six bedrooms (king, double, a bunk room sleeping four, queen, king, queen) and 4 baths, sleeps 14. A private pool with a recently redone pool area, fence not mentioned. The Ocean Park beach is about 5 minutes on foot, Barbosa Park 1 minute and the Calle Loíza cafes and bars about 8, with Kasalta and Pirilo a 2-minute drive. A backup generator, a 1,000-gallon cistern and air conditioning throughout. 9.0 out of 10 from 152 reviews.
houses.price: From $898 for one October night with taxes and fees on Vrbo. Our guess for the holiday week is $1,400 to $2,500 a night
houses.verdict: Ocean Park has more of a neighborhood feel, but the beach at its door faces the swell, so the calm swim would be a 10 to 15 minute drive. Maybe only if the Isla Verde houses are taken.

Main Street has shops, galleries, restaurants and the free trolley, and there'd be a hot tub at the house every night.

trips.name: Lake Placid
trips.place: The Olympic village, upstate New York
trips.pitch: The family's February base, again, but this time with a hot tub and the kids along. Main Street, the Mirror Lake loop, the Olympic Center and the skating oval are all walkable, Whiteface is twenty minutes by car, and everyone including Mom skied it last time. Two things to know as of October 21. The bobsled ride is listed as unavailable for track updates, and the walkable six-bedroom houses with hot tubs already show booked for the week.
why: The village is easy to walk, with Main Street shops and restaurants, the paved 2.7-mile Mirror Lake loop, outdoor skating on the Olympic oval, dog-sled rides on Mirror Lake daily from December 26, the Olympic Museum and the 1980 arena.

Whiteface, the mountain all five riders skied in February, has snowmaking on nearly every acre. Mom could do cross-country on the 1932 and 1980 Nordic trails at Mt Van Hoevenberg at the 70-and-up rate.
It's a drive instead of a flight day, about 10 hours 40 minutes from Virginia Beach with a night in the Hudson Valley on the way up, the way Patrick did it last time. Daniel would fly to Albany.
The Mirror Lake Inn spa, the Wild Center and the skating oval for the kids (Taylor skates free), and a hot tub for Mom.
Roughly $28,000 to $36,000 for ten with the one house we've confirmed is open.
catch: The bobsled, the main reason Kristina wanted to come back, can't be booked right now. The venue's page redirects and the tourism site says it's unavailable for track updates. The skeleton ride that is offered is ages 13 and up, so only the adults could go.

The walkable six-bedroom houses with hot tubs (Hillcrest Haven, the Stevens house, the Waterfront house) all show booked for December 27 to January 3. The one house confirmed open, Cliff View Loj, is under a mile out, which one reviewer called a 30-minute walk. Camp Kobl Hill could change the picture, but it needs a phone call.
It's cold, with highs near 28 degrees and nights near zero.
Ten to eleven hours of driving each way, and winter on I-87 and Route 73 can add hours.
The toboggan chute needs a foot of lake ice, which probably won't happen before January.
trips.weather: Reliably wintry with short days. December highs are about 28 degrees, nights near zero, and about 104 inches of snow a year. Whiteface has snowmaking across nearly all of its skiable acres.

notes.title: What about Stowe, Vermont?
paragraphs: Stowe has a house with a hot tub, a real spa at Topnotch or the Trapp Family Lodge, an Epic mountain for all five riders, and the groomed recreation path from the village. The drive is 12 to 13 hours from Virginia Beach, one to two more than Lake Placid. The village is small, so the house would need to be right in it to be walkable, and there's no bobsled. Roughly $26,000 to $42,000 for ten, with two six-bedroom hot-tub houses found and neither priced for the week yet.

getting_there.how: Drive 10 hours 41 minutes without stops by Google Maps, close to the 11 hours it took in February. Two cars, a night in the Hudson Valley on Saturday December 26, and check-in Sunday. Flying would be one stop to Albany (American through Philadelphia, United through Washington, Southwest through Baltimore), then about 2.5 hours north.

trips.name: Mont-Tremblant
trips.pitch: A car-free village at the base of the mountain, lit up at night, with the skating rink, the Aquaclub water park, the open-air Cabriolet gondola and two dozen restaurants on foot. The mountain is on the low side (about 750 to 2,900 feet) and it's on the Ikon pass. One six-bedroom house with a private hot tub is open and priced for our exact week. Getting there would be a one-connection flight to Montreal for each household, then 90 minutes to two hours of winter driving and a border. Nights run near 5 degrees.
why: A car-free village with heated walkways, a free lit skating rink with ice slides and free skate loans, the Cabriolet, sleigh rides from the village, and the Brind'O Aquaclub for a cold afternoon.
The Scandinave spa is ten minutes away, an outdoor thermal circuit where everyone keeps quiet.

Plenty to do besides skiing: dog sledding seven minutes away where kids can ride with the guide from age 3, guided snowmobiles, an ice-climbing intro, and 80 kilometers of Nordic trails at Domaine Saint-Bernard.
Tremblant's own advice for the holiday week is to start on the North Side and ride the upper lifts to skip the 10 AM South Side line, and January 1 is usually lighter.
Panache 784 is open and priced for December 27 to January 3, with six bedrooms and a private outdoor hot tub, about $27,900 to $31,000 for the week with fees.
catch: Every household would connect once to Montreal, then drive 90 minutes to two hours north in winter, probably after dark on arrival day, with a border each way.

The house is a shuttle ride from the village, not a walk. The listing says shuttle or a short drive, one guest calls it a 25-minute uphill hike, and another says it's a five-minute walk from the shuttle stop. This one probably only makes sense if we're fine using the free resort shuttle to get home.
Nights near 5 degrees and highs in the 20s, and wind can close the summit lifts.
There's no hospital in Mont-Tremblant. The nearest 24-hour ER is about 40 minutes away in Sainte-Agathe, so we'd want to bring epinephrine from home.
Roughly $45,000 to $66,000 for ten at the current exchange rate.
trips.weather: Real winter. December highs are about 27 degrees with lows about 14, and January highs are about 19 with lows about 5. Snow is likely. Wind can close the summit lifts and leave the lower half open.

notes.title: Money, in two currencies
paragraphs: Prices here are in US dollars at 1.42 Canadian dollars to the US dollar, the mid-October rate. The rate moved from 1.40 to 1.42 over the previous month, so the Canadian-priced lines could shift a few percent either way. Vrbo quotes in US dollars, and Airbnb and the local operators quote in Canadian dollars with about 18 percent of tax and resort royalty on activities.
Not in any line: the Kidz Club and Snow School, which don't publish prices and fill up months ahead for this week.

getting_there.how: No nonstop. One connection to Montreal on American through Philadelphia or Delta through LaGuardia, 4 to 8 hours. Sampled December fares ran $650 to $900, and the holiday week will likely be higher. US preclearance happens at Montreal on the way home.
One connection through LaGuardia, Newark, Washington or Philadelphia on Delta, United or American, about 4 to 6 hours.
Air Canada's Austin to Montreal nonstop started as a summer route and isn't confirmed for winter, so probably one stop through Detroit, Toronto, Atlanta or Fort Lauderdale.

About 125 kilometers on Autoroute 15 and Route 117, 90 minutes to two hours in winter. Two rental SUVs on winter tires (required in Quebec through March 15), with a grocery stop in Saint-Jovite. The Skyport coach runs from the airport Thursday to Sunday only, 9:30 AM daily and 3 PM on weekends, about $115 an adult round trip. That would work for a Sunday arrival, but we'd have no cars.
getting_there.est: $1,500 to $2,800 for two SUVs and fuel
